Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:38: Regarding the three keys, our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Zohar, Midrash HaNe'elam, Vayera 116b): these three the Holy One, blessed be He, did not give over to any agent, for Rabbi Simon said: come and see the power of the Holy One, blessed be He — in one instant He revives the dead, brings down to Sheol and raises up, causes lights to shine, makes grass grow, fattens crops, remembers the barren, gives sustenance, helps the poor, supports the fallen, straightens the bent, casts down kings and raises up kings — all at one time, in one moment, all at once, which no agent in the world could ever do. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:39: And in Devarim Rabbah, parashat Ki Tavo, on the verse (Deuteronomy 28:12), "The Lord will open for you His good treasury," they elaborated at length on the greatness of the key of rains, saying it is equal to the resurrection of the dead. And they said there, another interpretation: "the Lord will open for you" — Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov said: when rains descend, commerce is blessed, as it says, "to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the work of your hands." The Rabbis say: even the fish are blessed [by rain]; our sages told a story about this, etc. Another interpretation: "the Lord will open for you" — come and see how great is the descent of rain. Rabbi Yehudah bar Yechezkel, whenever he saw rain descending, would bless: may the Name of Him who spoke and the world came to be, be glorified, magnified, and blessed — He who appoints a thousand thousands and myriads upon myriads of angels over each and every drop that falls. Why? Because from here to the firmament is a five-hundred-year journey, and the rains descend, and no drop mingles with its fellow. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:40: In the key of sustenance there is a discernment by which to understand and know that there is one Creator who watches over its particulars and knows its affairs for its good. And were I to elaborate on what I heard from my teachers about miracles that occurred to individual people regarding sustenance, through Elijah, of blessed memory, I would depart from the subject of this exposition — and here in Safed, one such person is still alive today.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:41: <b>Our master, Rabbi Shlomo Alkabetz HaLevi, may his Rock protect him, composed a prayer concerning sustenance, to be recited every day, and wrote in it: "You are the God who feeds from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice, and no angel or prince has the power to feed, sustain, and provide for Your provision, as it is written by David Your servant (Psalms 145:15), 'The eyes of all look to You, and You give them their food in its time; You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing,' and it is written (ibid. 136:26), 'He gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever' — and this key is in Your hand, to refine and purify human beings so that they trust in You and know that there is no savior besides You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:42: With this the verse "the eyes of all look to You," etc., may be understood: "the eyes of all" includes all the worlds, upper and lower, that are below the Shechinah — for all of them await their life and their flow from her, since even the angels nurse daily sustenance from above, and likewise the supernal souls, as explained in parashat Terumah (Zohar 156b), and as we explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:43: Further, of God's kindness to man regarding his sustenance is His giving intellect, understanding, and knowledge to devise his livelihood through craft and stratagem — this is what the verse says (Deuteronomy 8:18), "and you shall say in your heart, my power and the strength of my hand have made me this wealth — but you shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you power to make wealth," which Onkelos renders: "for He gives you counsel to acquire possessions."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:44: Likewise it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, ch. 14): once I was traveling from place to place and a man found me who had Scripture but not Mishnah in his possession. He said to me: Rabbi, I will say something before you, but I fear you may take offense. I said to him: Heaven forbid, if you ask me about words of Torah. He said to me: Rabbi, why is it written (Psalms 136:25), "He gives bread to all flesh," and it is written (Psalms 147:9), "He gives to the beast its food" — but does not a person prepare his own bread? I said to him: this is the way of the world — one acts with his own hands, and the Holy One, blessed be He, blesses the work of his hands, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:29), "so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hand." Should one then sit idle? Scripture teaches, "which you shall do." He said to me: this answer is the very first approach I mentioned to you [i.e., he had already thought of it]. I said to him, my son, I will answer you: go and learn from the fool from whom wisdom has been taken — he cannot sustain himself for even one hour. Therefore, when people lose their intellect, they are considered like a beast, an animal, and a bird, and the Holy One, blessed be He, apportions sustenance to all who come into the world. — end of quotation. This is brought in the Yalkut (Psalms, mizmor 136, siman 883) on the verse "He gives bread to all flesh."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:45: And in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, parashah 15) it says, in these words: "Who has cleft a channel for the flood?" (Job 38:25) — Rabbi Berechiah said: there is a place where they call hair "flood." There was a story of a pious man who sat expounding: there is not a single hair for which the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create its own individual follicle, so that no one hair should benefit from its fellow. The next day he sought to go out to earn his livelihood. They said to him: yesterday you sat expounding that there is not a single hair for which the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create its own individual follicle so that no hair should benefit from another, and now you seek to go out to seek your livelihood? Sit, and your Creator will provide for you. He heard this, sat down, and his sustenance arose for him. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:46: In order to grasp the secret of this passage mentioned, you must know what is explained in the Tikkunim (67b) regarding [the teaching that] children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit but on mazal [the astral influence/root-source] — meaning that mazal is the first three sefirot: they say that "life" corresponds to Chochmah, "sustenance" to Binah, "children" to Da'at. And they said (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 103b): "and from there [come] life and sustenance and children. Life — 'and wisdom gives life to those who have it.' Sustenance — 'You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing' — and she is the Supernal Mother. Children — 'the son of Yah' — and this is the exalted hand, Binah, whose letters are Yod-Heh-Vav." — end of quotation. This is found in a manuscript, and in the printed edition it is along these lines, except that it says that "life" is Chochmah, flowing through the right thigh; "sustenance" is Binah, flowing through the left thigh; and "children" is in Tiferet. And because sustenance flows from the side of Imma [the Mother], the verse says (Job 38:25), "Who has cleft [MI] a channel for the flood," for the attribute of MI is what gives to each gate its own individual life-sustenance, and therefore of her it is said (Psalms 55:23), "Cast your burden upon the Lord," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:47: It may be said that the three keys mentioned correspond to children, life, and sustenance, which depend on mazal, where lies the secret of the "key" explained in parashat Bereishit; and therefore they are called "keys" and were not given over to an agent, because their dependence is on mazal. And when you grasp what is explained in the Tikkunim regarding "You open Your hand" (Psalms 145:16), you will see and understand that three worlds are rightly called three keys.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:48: If at times a person suffers difficulty in attaining his livelihood, by way of hardship, he should know that the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to discipline him with sufferings to cleanse him of his sins. And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote, also regarding food, when one discerns the sustenance of creatures according to their kinds, regarding the fly, food for the spider, and the like — what our sages, of blessed memory, expounded (Ketubot 49b, Tanchuma, Ekev 2) regarding (Psalms 147:9), "to the young ravens who cry" — that the young are white and their parents do not recognize them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on them and provides gnats out of their own excrement, which enter their mouths.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:49: And what they expounded (Midrash Tehillim, mizmor 42) regarding (Psalms 42:2), "As the hart pants after the water-brooks," in these words: "as the hart" [ke-ayal, masculine] pants — it does not say "ke-ayelet" [feminine] but "ke-ayal" [masculine], yet "pants" [ta'arog] is feminine. Why? Rather, this hind, when she crouches upon the birthstool, suffers and cries out [orget] to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He answers her and sends her a snake that bites her in the womb, and immediately the womb opens. So too the sons of Korach cried out from distress that they not perish, and He answered them; therefore it says "as the hart pants." What is meant by "after the water-brooks"? The hind is the most devoted of animals, and when the animals are thirsty they gather near the hind, and she digs and thrusts her horns into the ground and cries out to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He splits the deep for her and the waters rise up for her — this is "as the hart pants after the water-brooks." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:50: And what is written, "when she crouches upon the birthstool," etc., "a snake comes and bites her," etc. — so the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Beshalach 52b), and they elaborated further on the secret of the hind in parashat Pinchas (249b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:51: Further, on the matter of the discernment of sustenance, is what the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Beshalach 61b) regarding the four types of sustenance, which we shall quote in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15; from there one discerns that man does not live by bread alone, but by every utterance of the mouth of the Lord does man live.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:52: With this what we observe may be reconciled — how several penitents fast three days and three nights, and some have fasted four days and four nights, and some six, and did not die; whereas by the way of nature, a physician would say they endanger their lives — and similarly with the mortifications that penitents undertake while remaining healthy: all of it is divine assistance to them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:53: It may be that this is what David the king, peace be upon him, intended in saying (Psalms 136:25), "He gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever" — explaining that the Holy One, blessed be He, provides sustenance, called "bread," to all flesh according to its preparation: to one He provides bread that is coarse food; to the sick, food according to their preparation; and to Torah scholars, according to their preparation — for the essential sustenance of Torah scholars is Torah itself, as it says (Proverbs 9:5), "Come, eat of my bread." And so they explained in the Tikkunim (45b): when the Shechinah descends to bring forth abundance for her children, she brings down to each one sustenance fitting for him — to whom does she bring down the sustenance of Torah, which is the sustenance of the soul; to whom does she bring down the sustenance of the body — to each according to his desire. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:54: Further, one should reflect on how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, has done for him, and from how many mortal dangers He has saved him — for how many sick people reach the gates of death and are healed; and likewise how many are threatened by bandits and are not killed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:55: At times the Holy One, blessed be He, performs a miracle for a person and he does not recognize it, as is brought in the Midrash on the verse (Psalms 136:4), "To Him who alone does great wonders" — they asked, is it not obvious that the Holy One, blessed be He, does all things alone, without any partnership, Heaven forbid? They answered: rather, He alone knows what wonders He performs. How so? A person lies on his bed and a snake is before him on the ground; he rises to stand, and the snake senses him and slips away from before him — and he does not know what wonders the Holy One, blessed be He, has done for him, and who knows it? Only the Holy One, blessed be He. And so it says (Psalms 40:6), "Many things You have done, O Lord my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us — none can be compared to You; I would declare and speak of them, but they are too many to recount." Rabbi Elazar said: even the one for whom the miracle is performed does not recognize his own miracle, as it says "alone." And as Rav Yosef expounded on what is written (Isaiah 12:1), "I will thank You, O Lord, for though You were angry with me" — of what does the verse speak? Of two men who went on a business trip; a thorn pierced the foot of one of them, and he began cursing and blaspheming. Some days later he heard that his companion's ship had sunk at sea, and he began to give thanks and praise; therefore it says, "Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:56: Now, among the things a person must contemplate in his mind as being of the providence of the Holy One, blessed be He, over man is the matter of dreams — for through them a person may examine his deeds, as we quoted the words of the Rashbi, peace be upon him, in parashat Chayei Sarah, in chapter 4 of the Gate of Holiness — for according to one's deeds, so is he shown in a dream, as Elihu said (Job 33:15), "in a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men... then He opens the ears of men." And this thing is seen sensibly, that according to what a man is, so his dreams are true; and at times he will see visions in the upper world and speak with the dead and recognize them, and they will reveal to him matters of Gan Eden and Gehinnom, as has happened in our times in several stories — but I have not come in this composition to elaborate on the telling of such stories.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:57: Our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot ch. 2, 14b) that one who goes seven days without a dream is called wicked, in these words: Rabbi Yonah said in the name of Rabbi Zeira: whoever lodges seven days without a dream is called wicked, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "he who is satisfied [save'a] shall lodge untouched by evil" — do not read "save'a" [satisfied] but "sheva" [seven]. — end of quotation. Rashi, of blessed memory, explained that because he is wicked, Heaven does not attend to him to visit him with a dream. It occurs to me that because his soul does not ascend above, therefore it does not come to him, for he resembles the animal spirit that descends below, to the earth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:58: Likewise, through dreams the decrees issued in the upper world become known; and the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Shemot 6b) that when there are meritorious ones in the generation, the decree is made known to the head of the generation, and if not, to people lacking understanding or to children, in these words: Rabbi Chiya said: thirty days before might comes upon the world in the land, or before calamity comes upon a people in the land, this matter is proclaimed in the world; sometimes this matter is conveyed through the mouth of children, sometimes to people who have no understanding, and sometimes this matter is conveyed through the mouths of birds and proclaimed in the world, and no one pays attention to them. When the people are meritorious, this matter is conveyed to the meritorious heads of the world, so that they may know it and return to their Master; and when they are not meritorious, it is as stated [to lesser vessels]. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:59: Another thing a person must contemplate with his intellect regarding the Holy One, blessed be He's, providence over Israel is when he discerns the matter of wisdom given by Him, blessed be He, to those fit for it, as our sages, of blessed memory, said: one who sees the sages of Israel blesses, "Blessed is He who has given a portion of His wisdom to those who fear Him" — and indeed we have seen here in Safed, in the Upper Galilee, sages for whom this blessing was truly fitting to say. We have also seen sages expert in the wisdom of discerning the face [physiognomy], able to tell a person all that he has done, whether good or bad — and surely they merited this wondrous wisdom, which is close to the holy spirit, only on account of their deeds and their piety.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:60: Also of this category of contemplation is the wisdom of Kabbalah in the workings of the holy names, which perform several actions through the Name of Forty-Two Letters and the Name of Seventy-Two — and the Rashbi, peace be upon him, so explained (parashat Beha'alotcha 151a) regarding the Name of Seventy-Two, in these words: "And in this name is the binding of the Patriarchs; paths are found for judgment and for mercy, for assistance, for kindness, for fear, for Torah, for life, for death, for good and for evil. Fortunate are the righteous who know the paths of Torah and know how to walk in the Torah of the Holy King." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:61: Although the truth is that it is not fitting for every person to make use of the holy names — for who is fit to use the king's scepter except one who is close to the king — nevertheless we know for certain, without doubt, that one who knows how to use them and is fit to do so may perform awesome actions, as I have seen and as I have heard from the mouth of one who performed them. The Name of Seventy-Two derives from the verses "and it journeyed," "and it came," and "and it stretched out" (Exodus 14:19-21), and it is the Name by which the sea was split, and therefore it is mentioned here. There is also the Explicit Name mentioned in connection with the celestial spheres and their rotation, which performs even greater wonders.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:62: Further, among the matters of contemplation that arouse a person to know his Creator and to perform His Torah and commandments is the contemplation of the matter of death — for death in man is not like death in other living creatures. For in other creatures, if they die a natural death, the matter stems from illness, such as an animal that is treifah [fatally injured] and cannot live, or the exhaustion of powers due to old age. But the matter of death is not so with man — for we find death occurring in small children, and likewise in young men whose strength is whole and who are in their vigor and might, who die a sudden death without any preceding cause of illness at all; especially in the illness of plague, which is sent from Him, blessed be He, for our sins from time to time, in which youth and old and women die without cause, and in this illness the understanding of physicians becomes confused, none of them knowing good from bad — for we find that a physician will say, regarding this illness, that the patient is well, and within an hour or two he dies. And many afflicted by plague see the angel of destruction, some seeing a sword, some a bow and arrows, and the like — as we have seen here in Safed, in the Upper Galilee, many times, for at a time of plague, due to the great judgment, the agents of judgment take on visible form so that they can be seen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:63: You should know that death, for Israel in particular, is a supernal kindness to them for the rectification of their souls, and therefore it is said of Him (Psalms 145:17), "and kind in all His deeds" — for His principal deeds are the souls, which are truly the work of His hands. This is: when the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that this body, built jointly by a man and his wife — for they contain flesh from the side of the kelipot — no longer serves any purpose for the fulfillment of the commandments, He nullifies its existence in order to benefit the rectification of His portion, which is the soul. For if there were no rectification, what benefit would it be to the Holy One, blessed be He, to kill it and nullify its existence from the world? And why create it in the first place, if He is only going to kill it after some years? Rather, surely this is the secret of reincarnation (which our sages, of blessed memory, taught us, and Pythagoras agreed with them, although many disagree with this view) — in which His thoughts run deep, for He devised plans so that no one banished from Him should remain banished. The Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul into this world to see whether it will improve its deeds, and lets it remain until it accomplishes the rectification of that matter for which it was sent, and if it does not rectify it, they cut it down, as a tree that bears no fruit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:64: Regarding the rectification of death for Israel, that it is a good thing for them, the prophet said (Jeremiah 18:6), "Behold, as clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel" — for the potter, when he sees that the vessel is not coming out properly, nullifies the form of that clay from what it was and shapes it into another, more perfect form. So too, regarding the secret of reincarnation, it is said (Job 14:20), "You change his countenance and send him away" — for if his countenance was originally the face of a lion, he will come in a second incarnation with the face of an ox, and so on for the others; and always the divine intention is to rectify souls in the manner fitting for them. For if this were not the divine intention regarding death, for the rectification of souls, it would be difficult [to understand] — for is it fitting that a craftsman who makes a perfected work, and after completing its making, which he labored over, should then decide to destroy it? Would we not say his teeth are blunted [i.e., that he is a fool], that he is not of sound mind — unless it be said that its destruction in this form is in order to make it in another, more excellent form. So too the matter is with this craft that the Holy One, blessed be He, fashioned, as it says (Deuteronomy 32:6), "He made you and established you" — made and built with His supernal wisdom out of the totality of all the worlds; for if there were no rectification in nullifying its existence from this world, He would not put it to death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:65: And everything is conducted according to how those below conduct themselves: if those below prepare their deeds properly, the Shechinah, called the "wheel" through which souls are reincarnated, tips to the right side, and the world is rectified; and if not, Heaven forbid, it tips to the left side, as explained by the elder [Sabba] (Zohar, parashat Mishpatim 95b), that the scale never rests, and souls ascend, enter, and return; and he says further there, and when the people of the world conduct themselves on the side of good, the scale stands and tips to the side of good, and when they conduct themselves toward evil, it tips to that side; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:66: In this manner too the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (ibid., parashat Vayera 109b) the verse (Job 37:12), "And He turns about by His guidance," etc. Our sages, of blessed memory, said: Rabbi Elazar said, "He turns about" — the Holy One, blessed be He, causes circumstances to circle about and brings deeds into the world to be sustained, and afterward, when people think that those deeds will be sustained, the Holy One, blessed be He, overturns those deeds from how they were at first. "By His guidance" — it is written "betachbulotav" [with defective spelling] — like a craftsman who makes clay vessels: while that wheel is spinning before him, he thinks to make a certain shape and does so, then thinks to make another shape and does so, turning one vessel into another, because that wheel is spinning before him. So the Holy One, blessed be He, overturns His deeds which He performs — "betachbulotav," [written] lacking the yod — and what is this? This is the court of judgment below, which is the wheel spinning before Him; therefore He turns the vessels from one to another, and all this is according to the deeds of human beings. If people improve their deeds, that spinning wheel turns them to the right, and then deeds are performed in the world to benefit them as is fitting, and the wheel spins constantly on that right side, and the world is rolled along by it. If people come to do evil, His guidance, which spins constantly and stands in the spinning of the right, the Holy One, blessed be He, turns it to the left side, and overturns the circumstances and vessels that were originally toward that left side, and then the wheel spins and deeds are performed in the world to harm those people, and the wheel spins to that side until people return to improve their deeds, and the wheel stands upon the deeds of people, and therefore "by His guidance" [betachbulotav] — for their action — and it does not remain constant. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:67: Through this passage, the saying of our sages, of blessed memory (Kiddushin ch. 8, 40b), may be understood: a person should always view himself as half meritorious and half guilty, and the world as half meritorious and half guilty; if he performs one commandment, happy is he, for he has tipped himself and the whole world to the scale of merit, etc. — and this tipping depends on the wheel mentioned, and it depends on the deeds of those below, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:68: Therefore, one who returns in repentance does kindness with his own soul, with his body, with the whole world — whom he tips to the scale of merit — and with the Holy One, blessed be He. With his soul — for he removes it from the judgment of Gehinnom and the other reckonings and judgments explained in the rest of the Gate of Fear, and from the judgment of reincarnation, which is hard for the soul. With his body — for he will not be cut off in the prime of his days, with the demand made of him, why did you not rectify your deeds, and perhaps you would have had a son who would be a halachic authority in Israel — so it is explained in Sefer HaBahir. And with the Holy One, blessed be He — for he does not burden the Holy One, blessed be He, to have to execute upon him the judgment of death and reincarnation, for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not desire the death of the wicked but that they turn from their evil ways — for the judgment of reincarnation is very hard for the soul, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is merciful, and His way is to do good to His creatures, especially to His holy souls, which are a part of Him, blessed be He, and He does not wish to uproot the soul from the place from which it was hewn, its original quarry, where its vital station is — this being like one who uproots a tree from its original place of planting and from its roots, where it lived, and transplants it elsewhere. For this reason the Holy One, blessed be He, is patient with the wicked, that perhaps they will repent, for the choice is in their hands, and when He sees that they have not repented, then He uproots them in order to transplant them elsewhere. This subject is elaborated at length in the Tikkunim (102b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:69: Therefore the discerning person is obligated to contemplate the matter of death, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 7:4), "the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning," "and let the living take it to heart" (ibid. v. 2) — for one was not sent into this world to eat and drink like an animal, in the manner of fools whose heart is in the house of feasting, for to this end what benefit would there be in his creation? Indeed there are many of this sort among the idol-worshiping nations who eat and drink and do their work and die, and "as they came, so they go," and they are not punished, because they have no [immortal] soul [in this sense] and were not commanded regarding the commandments — except if they act wickedly, in which case it is said of them (I Samuel 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies He shall sling out as from the pocket of a sling."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:70: The Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar Chadash on Song of Songs (70d) that one of the things a person must give account of at his passing is whether he inquired and knew why his soul came into the world and what it came to rectify, in these words: "There is wisdom that a person needs — one, to know and contemplate the secrets of his Master; [and one] to know his own body and to know who he is, how he was created, from where he comes and to where he goes, and how the rectification of his body is to be rectified, and how he is destined to enter into judgment before the King of all; and one, to know and contemplate the secrets of his soul — who is that soul within him, from where does it come, and for what purpose does it come into this body, a foul drop, here today and tomorrow in the grave." — end of quotation, as it pertains to our subject.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:71: Further, on the matter of the rectification that death brings to man, being the rectification of his soul, the Rashbi, peace be upon him, elaborated (Zohar, parashat Terumah 150a). He raised a difficulty there regarding what our sages, of blessed memory, said on the verse, "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good [tov me'od]" — "tov" [good] is the angel of life, and "me'od" [very] is the angel of death, who is even better, since he obeys the command of his Master. And he elaborated at length in resolving the matter, regarding Gan Eden and the matter of Adam before his sin. In brief, his intent regarding this matter is that through Adam's sin, man became clothed in the coarse material body which prevents the soul from gazing upon the supernal spiritual realities; and through death he sheds this garment and becomes clothed in a spiritual garment made from the Torah and the commandments he engaged in in this world, and through these he merits to gaze upon and delight in the light of the supernal life. And he said: "and the Holy One, blessed be He, does a kindness with His creatures, that a person is not stripped of these [earthly] garments until other garments, more precious and better than these, have been prepared for him — except for those wicked of the world who did not return in complete repentance to their Master, for they came into the world naked and naked they shall return there." — end of quotation. It follows that death is a rectification for the righteous person, in that through it he merits to be clothed in that spiritual garment; and for the wicked person, in that from fear of death he will return in repentance, as we explained there above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:72: Of this same category of contemplation is discerning what we find, that several righteous men were not subject to the worm [after death] — and besides those mentioned in the baraita (Bava Batra 17a), we find Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Bava Metzia ch. 7, 83b), and the Rashbi, peace be upon him, as is evident in the Zohar (parashat Bereishit 4a). And likewise in the time of the Amoraim, Achai bar Yoshiah, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat ch. 23, 152b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:73: And even in our own times, in the kingdom of Fez, a similar incident occurred, and this is how it happened: a pious man passed away outside his own town, in a village a day or two's journey away, and was buried there. After several years, the sons of that pious man went to bring back his bones to be buried with his family, and they found that his flesh had not decomposed except for one leg. His eldest son was troubled over this matter, as to what cause had led that leg to decompose, and he worried lest the worm still afflict it, and he fasted [seeking an answer]. His father came to him in a dream and said to him: know that the worm did not afflict me except in that leg, because I once kicked a Torah scholar with it; but the rest of my body, in which I did not sin, was not afflicted by the worm and never will be. So I heard from an elderly sage who heard these words from the son of the aforementioned pious man himself, and his son is still alive.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:74: When a person contemplates this matter, he will see that for this generation it is a great thing indeed, and without doubt everything depends only on deeds, as it is said (Avot 1:17), "study is not the essential thing, but rather action" — for there are many students of Torah who have not merited this, and everything depends on how a person purifies his soul and his deeds; accordingly his physical matter is purified and the worm does not rule over it. And it may be that for this reason the righteous, at their death, are called "living" — because they purified their soul from the filth of the serpent, which is jealousy, desire, and honor-seeking, and therefore the accursed serpent, from whose side comes the worm, had no power over them; rather, the power of Torah and commandments, called "life," clung to that flesh to some degree, so that the worm could not rule over it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:75: This is the divine intent regarding death: that the sin of the first man be rectified, and the matter return to what it was at the time of creation, when the sphere of Adam's heel outshone the sphere of the sun, as they explained in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, parashat Acharei Mot 20:2), in these words: Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: the heel of the first man outshone the sphere of the sun — how much more so the countenance of his face! And do not be surprised — it is the way of the world that a person makes one bag for himself and one for his household; for whom does he make the finer one? Is it not for himself? So too, the first man was created for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, while the sphere of the sun was created for the service of creatures. — end of quotation. And so they explained in the Tikkunim (10b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:76: They further explained (Zohar, parashat Chayei Sarah, Midrash HaNe'elam 121b): come and see, Rabbi Yehudah said: the form and beauty of the first man was like the splendor of the supernal firmament that is above all the other firmaments, and like that light which the Holy One, blessed be He, has hidden away for the righteous for the World to Come. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:77: Regarding the resurrection of the dead, this matter shall be rectified, as they explained there. And so our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yalkut, parashat Devarim, siman 801) that the righteous are destined in the future to be like the sun and the moon, etc. And so they said in the Zohar in parashat Bereishit (Zohar, parashat Bereishit 4a) about the Rashbi, when Rabbi Chiya saw him, saying there: he saw that they were being renewed and returned to their splendor and light, greater than the light of the splendor of the sun. — end of quotation.
